Robin Roefs" penalty saves secures Sunderland's spot in FA Cup fourth round

Get the Adam Clery Football Column. A newsletter that unpacks the absurdities and oddities of the beautiful game

The ACFC newsletter: unpacking football's absurdities

Unpack football's oddities with the ACFC newsletter

Robin Roefs was Sunderland's hero as Everton's FA Cup hopes came to a premature end once again after three woeful penalties in a shootout saw the Black Cats reach round four.

David Moyes" threadbare squad looked like exiting in normal time until James Garner's 89th-minute spot-kick cancelled out Enzo Le Fee's brilliant first-half strike.

But extra time was the last thing the hosts, down to just 12 senior players, needed and when the shootout came around Garner, Thierno Barry and Beto all saw their efforts saved by Roefs.

Le Fee, Granit Xhaka and Luke O'Nien confidently scored their first three attempts to help Sunderland into the fourth round for only the second time in 11 seasons.

It was a hammer blow to Everton, who were dragged back into the game by Adam Aznou, a £7.8million signing from Valladolid in the summer who had not had a sniff of first-team action.

The teenager's only senior football was two appearances in the EFL Trophy back in September and October and his 86th-minute introduction for Merlin Rohl was only because Moyes had little to no option.

But the Spanish-born Moroccan showed more drive in the four minutes of regulation time than many of his battle-weary team-mates had in the preceding 86 - particularly fellow 19-year-old and summer arrival Tyler Dibling, who cost five times as much.

Within three minutes he won an admittedly soft penalty after a shoulder-to-shoulder challenge by Trai Hume allowing Garner to equalise.

Replays of the foul on the big screens at full-time enraged Xhaka, who hurled his water bottle into the turf and raged at the perceived injustice to anyone in earshot, but the Black Cats" captain was soon celebrating.

It is rare for Sunderland, promoted from the Championship last season, to be favourites in any game but the fact Regis Le Bris was able to make five changes and still have the likes of Dan Ballard, Brian Brobbey, Omar Alderete and Wilson Isidor in reserve swung the odds in their favour.

Injuries, the Africa Cup of Nations and suspensions for Michael Keane and Jack Grealish were compounded by Tim Iroegbunam's hamstring problem which took the absences to nine.

Barry, the one senior player he left out, accounted for 23 of the 27 first-team appearances among the substitutes with five of six academy players not having previously featured at all.

After Harrison Armstrong sliced wide their only first chance of the first half, Sunderland took control and should have been comfortably ahead by the interval.

Their first shot resulted in the opener - and what a goal.

Everton failed to deal with a long throw and Eliezer Mayenda teed up Le Fee to send a cushioned right-footed volley curling past Jordan Pickford.

Moyes had a face like thunder and his demeanour was not improved as Pickford clawed away a Nordi Mukiele overhead kick and tipped away, at full-stretch, Romaine Mundle's strike from distance.

Surprisingly, the Everton boss did not make the only change available to him and sacrifice one of his five midfielders for Barry at the start of the second half, but they did not come to life until Mayenda rolled an angled shot just wide with less than half an hour remaining.

Beto's appeal for a penalty for a shirt pull by Hume was waved away but referee John Brooks obliged when Aznou went down and Garner equalised.

Unfortunately for Everton their subsequent penalties were not as confident, with Barry and Beto's stuttering run-ups far from convincing, as Roefs saved all three.

Čilge jalkaspálla erenomášvuođaid ACFC-dieđáhusreivve bokte

Robin Roefs lei Sunderlanda hero, go Evertona doaivvat FA Cupas fas nohkejedje ovdal áiggi, dan maŋŋel go golbma heittot penalteačuohcama torjeduvvojedje báhččemis ja Black Cats beasai njealját vurrii.

David Moyesa geahpes joavku orui leat jáhkkimin olggos juo dábálaš spealáiggi siste, ovdal go James Garnera 89. minuhta penaltea dássidii dili ja gomihii Enzo Le Fee čáppis vuosttaš beale golu.

Muhto lasseáigi lei maŋimuš maid ruovttubealli, geas ledje dušše 12 boarrásit speaddji, dárbbašii, ja go penalteabáhččen bođii, de Garner, Thierno Barry ja Beto buohkat oidne ahte Roefs torjjui sin geahččalusaid.

Le Fee, Granit Xhaka ja Luke O'Nien skorejedje vissásit iežaset vuosttaš golbma geahččalusa, ja veahkehedje Sunderlanda njealját vurrii dušše nuppe háve 11 jagi siste.

Dat lei garra čoavdda Evertonii, mii geassejuvvui ruovttoluotta speallui Adam Aznou bokte, geasse 7,8 miljovnna poandda ovdii Valladolidas oasttihuvvon spēlariin, guhte ii lean oažžun makkárge vejolašvuođa vuosttašjoavkkus.

Nuorra spēlarii áidna boarrásit dási jalkaspálla lei guokte oassálastima EFL Trophy:s čakčamánu ja golggotmánu, ja su 86. minuhta sisaboahtin Merlin Rohl sadjái dáhpáhuvai dušše danne go Moyesii ii lean eará molssaevttut.

Muhto Spánias riegádan marokkoláš čájehii eanet roahkkatvuođa dan njeallje dábálaš spealminuhta áigge go máŋggat su soađđeváibman joavkobártnit ovddit 86 minuhta áigge – erenoamážit nubbi 19-jahkásaš geasseboahtán Tyler Dibling, geasa haddi lei vihtta geardde stuorát.

Golmma minuhta siste son vuittii, duođaid veahá geahpas, penaltea maŋŋel go Trai Hume válddii su badjelas-badjelii, ja dat attii Garnerii vejolašvuođa dássedit.

Go meattáhusdiliid ođđasčájehusat čájehuvvojedje stuorašearppain spealu loahpas, de dat suhttadii Xhaka, guhte bálkkihii čáhcebohtala eatnamii ja hárrii dan maid son oinnii eahpedivrrasvuohtan buot gullevaččaide, muhto Black Catsa kapitána ávvudii fargga maŋŋá.

Ii leat dábálaš ahte Sunderland, mii bajásmannai Championshipas mannan jagi, lea suosihuvvon mihkkege spealus, muhto dat ahte Regis Le Bris sáhtii dahkat vihtta rievdadusa ja vel leat várres Dan Ballard, Brian Brobbey, Omar Alderete ja Wilson Isidor lágan spēlariid, jorggihii vejolašvuođaid sin beallái.

Váttisvuođat, Africa Cup of Nations ja Michael Keane ja Jack Grealish gildosiid geavaheapmi lasihedje váttisvuođaid, ja Tim Iroegbunama čuovgagáttiváttisvuohta loktii eretorrunid ovcci dásái.

Barry, dat áidna boarrásit spēlarii gean son guođii olggobeallái, lei 23:s 27 vuosttašjoavkko oassálastimis molssaevttuid gaskkas, go guđa akademiijaspeaddjis vihtta eai lean ovdal oassálastán ollenge.

Maŋŋel go Harrison Armstrong čuohppii meattá sin áidna árrat vejolašvuođa vuosttaš beales, de Sunderland válddii spealu stivrrema ja galggai leat čielga jođus gaskaboddii.

Sin vuosttaš šuhtti addii rabasgolu – ja makkár golu dat lei.

Everton ii hálddašan guhkes sisabáhččema, ja Eliezer Mayenda ráhkadii Le Feeii vejolašvuođa sáddet čábbát olgešjuolggi volley-šuhttima joraheamen Jordan Pickforda meattá.

Moyesa muoto lei dego dárkilmu, ja son ii šaddan buoret mielas go Pickford torjjui Nordi Mukiele badjelguvlui báhččema ja, olles guhkodagas, guođii eret Romaine Mundle guhkesgaskka šuhttima.

Oainnatkeahtes Evertona hoavda ii dahkan áidna rievdadusa mii sus lei vejolaš, iige váldán ovtta su viđa gaskagiettispeaddjis eret Barry ovddas nuppe beale álggus, muhto sii eai ealáskan ovdal go Mayenda rollingii čohkkás guovttebealat šuhttima veahá meattá, go unnit go beađde diibmu lei báhcán.

Beto gáibádus penalteii Hume bustegeassima geažil hilgojuvvui, muhto duopmár John Brooks čujuhii báhččenbáikái go Aznou gahčai, ja Garner dássidii.

Evertona dáfus heađut eai leat sin maŋit penalteat leamaš seammá vissásat, go sihke Barry ja Beto geahččalusat álge eahpesihkkaris vuohkái, ja Roefs torjjui buot golmma.

source_doc:
I expected to love Project Hail Mary, I LOVED Project Hail Mary, it also destroyed me in a particularly unique way as the wife of a science teacher after a year of watching all science teaching be relentlessly attacked and defunded. People love this movie, which I'm sure will be a success, and they hate my wife's work and destroy her programs and want us to lose our careers. How is it possible for all this to be true at once.

She left at 7am to go teach the hands on labs that she teaches where they handle cells, where they've increased class sizes and reduced TAs, she spends more contact hours with students in lab basements than any other class on the campus. She created a program for community college transfer students to get funded jobs in labs, opening up STEM pathways for those who never would've gotten the chance. For all her above and beyond work she's demonized as "doing DEI in science" which they call illegal

But you know, I guess if she were a white male software engineer writing fanfic about science teaching.... she'd be safe.

@grimalkina the same roots are already in Hail Mary tbh. I like Andy Weir a lot and I don't think he meant it, but the whole "bureaucracy and cooperation are truly the barrier to getting things done, and when shit hits the fan we get a powerful anti-bureaucrat to forego diplomacy and strongarm everyone into doing the project, ethics or what the participants want be damned" struck me as a very American individualism power fantasy, and I would guess an American wrote it if I didn't know

@jcachada @grimalkina
For what it's worth, the book contains this passage that didn't make it to the movie.
---
“I’m curious,” I say to Stratt. “Once we launch Hail Mary. What will you do then?”
“Me?” she said. “Doesn’t matter. Once the Hail Mary launches, my authority ends. I’ll probably be put on trial by a bunch of pissed-off governments for abuse of power. Might spend the rest of my life in jail.”
“I’ll be in the cell next to you,” said Leclerc.
“Are you at all concerned about that?”
She shrugged. “We all have to make sacrifices. If I have to be the world’s whipping boy to secure our salvation, then that’s my sacrifice to make.”
---
Is she better or worse if she thinks she's sacrificing herself?

Son ásahii prográmma loahpahanstudeanttaide vai sii ožžot ruhtaduvvon bargguid laboratoriain, mii rahpá STEM-bálgáid sidjiide geat eai goasge eará láhkai livčče ožžon dán vejolašvuođa. US bound Thompson stars as Galway reach FBD final

California-bound Matthew Thompson lashed home 2-06 as Galway overcame Leitrim by 11 points in Tuam to book their spot in next week's FBD League decider.

2025 Young Footballer of the Year nominee Thompson will be out of action for the entirety of the league and the early part of the championship, with Padraic Joyce confirming that the Salthill-Knocknacarra players is studying in Berkeley for the upcoming semester.

He was the leading figure on a largely experimental Galway side - which also contained Cian Hernon and Kieran Molloy - as they came from three points down at half-time to beat Leitrim.

Thompson buried a goal in the top corner in the first half but the Connacht champions trailed Leitrim at the break, Killian Gaffney proving effective from placed balls, while Ryan O'Rourke and Jack Kelly also landed points.

Galway manager Padraic Joyce remonstrates with the referee over a decision

However, with Thompson converting a second half penalty, Galway eased home after the interval, with 10 different scorers overall as they ran out 2-19 to 0-14 winners.

After two rounds of the FBD League, the top two progress to next week's final, with Galway facing the winner of tomorrow's Roscommon-Mayo tie.

In Leinster, Westmeath have booked their spot in the O'Byrne Cup final after an 11-point win over Offaly in a goal-fest in Mullingar.

Waiting for them in the decider is a Kildare outfit that defeated Dublin 1-22 to 1-13.

Mark McHugh's Westmeath side advanced ahead of reigning champions Longford following a coin toss last Saturday but they impressed on the field of play on Saturday.

A brace of goals apiece from Danny McCarton and Brandon Kelly, plus another from Senan Baker, saw them run out 5-10 to 2-08 winners.

Ciaran Murphy scored two goals either side of half-time to pull the visitors back into the contest, the margin being briefly reduced to three points 11 minutes into the second half.

However, an unanswered burst of 3-02 over the next 15 minutes saw the hosts settle the contest in an emphatic manner.

Kildare found their feet in the second half against Dublin and now are one game away from a first O'Byrne Cup since 2014.

Harry O'Neill fires to the net for Kildare

Both management teams experimented in Newbridge with Dublin in particular shorn of overly familiar faces, but in the first half it seemed to matter little as they led 1-08 to 0-08 at the break.

Jamie McCarville palmed home their goal but it was Clyde Burke who caught the eye for the travelling support with some brilliant shooting that included two orange flags - the second of which was of the highest quality.

Alex Beirne was racking up the scores for the Lilywhites though and his two-point free early in the second half kick-started a run of 1-05 without reply, Harry O'Neill with the goal in the 43rd minute.

Kildare continued to turn the screw with James Harris' late two-pointer sending them on their way.

hypothesis:
USA:i vuolgi Thompson čuovvola, go Galway beassá FBD-finalii

Californiai vuolgi Matthew Thompson skoraidii 2-06, go Galway vuoitii Leitrima 11 čuoggáin Tuamis ja sihkkarasttii saji boahtte vahku FBD League-finalas.

Thompson, guhte lea evttohuvvon 2025 jagi nuorra jalkaspálli bálkkašupmái, ii galgga speallat olles liigga áigge eaige čempionáhta álgooasis, go Padraic Joyce nanne ahte Salthill-Knocknacarra-spiller oahppá Berkeley:s boahtte semeasteris.

Son lei ovddemus figuvra eanet geahččaleaddji Galway-joavkkus – mas ledje maiddái Cian Hernon ja Kieran Molloy – go sii geasuidedje iežaset golmma čuoggá duohken bealleáiggis ja vuoite Leitrima.

Thompson skoraidii vuosttaš bealis goalu alimus čiegahkii, muhto Connacht-measterat ledje bealleáiggi loahpas Leitrima maŋis; Killian Gaffney čájehii buori beaktilvuođa bidjonspárttain, ja Ryan O'Rourke ja Jack Kelly lasiheigga maid čuoggáid.

Galway-hoavda Padraic Joyce váidal duopmáriin mearrádusa geažil

Muhto go Thompson čađahii rihkusdákka nuppi bealis, de Galway válddii spealu iežas háldui bealleáiggi maŋŋel, ja go oppalaččat 10 iešguđet skoraideaddji ledje mielde, sii vuoite loahpas 2-19 vuostá 0-14.

Guovtti FBD League-vuoru maŋŋel beassaba guovtte buoremusat joavkkut boahtte vahku finalii, ja Galway deaivvada doppe ihttin Roscommon-Mayo-spealu vuoitejiin.

Leinsteris lea Westmeath sihkkarastan saji O'Byrne Cup-finalas maŋŋel go vuoitii Offaly 11 čuoggáin goalurikkis spealus Mullingaris.

Sin vuordá mearrideaddji spealus Kildare-joavku, mii vuoitii Dublina 1-22 vuostá 1-13.

Mark McHugh Westmeath-joavku beasai ovddos measta Longforda ovddabealde ruđaskruvnna bokte mannan lauvvardaga, muhto dán lauvvardaga sii váikkuhedje gieddes hui bures.

Danny McCarton ja Brandon Kelly skoraideigga goabbáge guokte goalu, ja Senan Baker lasihii vel ovtta, ja dain Westmeath vuoitii 5-10 vuostá 2-08.

Ciaran Murphy skoraidii guokte goalu, okta ovdal bealleáiggi ja okta dan maŋŋel, ja dat veahkehii guossiid ruovttoluotta gilvui; erohus unniduvvui oanehaččat golmma čuoggái 11 minuhta nuppi bealis.

Muhto čuovvovaš 15 minuhta sisa skoraidedje ruovttoluottat 3-02 vástádusa haga, ja danin sii mearridedje spealu čielgasit ja nannosit.

Kildare oaččui buoret doaibmama nuppi bealis Dublin vuostá, ja dál lea dušše okta speallu eret vuosttaš O'Byrne Cupas jagi 2014 rájes.

Harry O'Neill skoraida fierpmádahkii Kildare ovddas

Goappašat hoavddajoavkkut geahččaledje Newbridge:s iešguđetlágan čoahkkádusaid, ja erenoamážit Dublinis váiluhedje máŋga dábálaš nama, muhto vuosttaš bealis dat ii orron stuorra mearkkašumis go sii jođihe bealleáiggi loahpas 1-08 vuostá 0-08.

Jamie McCarville bálbii sin goalu ruoktot, muhto Clyde Burke geasuhii mátkki doarjjuid fuomášumi čábbát skoraideamiin, masa gulle maiddái guokte guovtti čuoggá skori – maŋimuš dain lei hui alla kvalitehta.

Alex Beirne čohkkehii gal čuoggáid Lilywhites-joavkui, ja su guovtti čuoggá friispeallu nuppi beale álggus álggahii 1-05 ráiddu vástádusa haga; Harry O'Neill skoraidii goalu 43. minuhtas.

Kildare joatkkai vel garrasit deaddilit vuosttáldaga, go James Harris maŋit guovtti čuoggá skori addii sidjiide buori loahpafártui.

$partner has a video consult with Ikea to quote for a fitted kitchen. It's a fascinating glimpse into the ecosystem of online services for boomers.
1. They send link for video consult, three weeks ago. It uses Ikea's proprietary videoconf solution

4. We dial in today, they start the call with "our system blocked your files, let's design your kitchen together"
1/x

5. Partner asks if there's any way to share the (very detailed, took us like a full man week to put together) designs, but the Ikea salesdrone is on a script, and isn't having a bar of it.
6. The next step in the script is "laboriously do the design from scratch over the phone with the client, hunting and pecking on the keyboard and not fast using the UI of their design software"
2/x

7. They cannot share their screen, so it's a clown show of repeated misunderstanding about which part of which image is being referred to

8. the clock has just ticked past what should have been the full consult, and they're 35% the way thru getting the required measurements.

9. So far there's been literally 8 minutes of salesdrone laboriously inputting the measurements supplied

source_doc:
Melbourne Renegades host Glenn Maxwell and the Melbourne Stars at Marvel Stadium in BBL15 after Usman Khawaja and Brisbane Heat host Sydney Thunder

Sam Harper dominated with 82 not out off 51 balls and Glenn Maxwell recalled the feeling of ball on bat in a subdued innings of 20 not out off 17 balls, which included one massive six. He has not lost his ability and would have enjoyed the chance to spend time in the middle.

The crowd of 42,846 was not given the contest they hoped for as the Stars won the match by eight wickets with 25 balls remaining.

It keeps Melbourne Stars in contention as they break a three-match losing sequence and makes life hard for Melbourne Renegades. Marcus Stoinis bowled well to take 3-33 and was on a hat-trick at one stage while Harper is in great form having hit 356 runs at a strike rate of 159 for the tournament. He was man-of-the-match.

Tom Rogers bounced back with a fast 50 against Melbourne Renegades

But it was all over once Tom Rogers helped himself to 50 off 19 balls to start the innings with an opening partnership of 84 with Harper.

"They outplayed us at the "G so it was nice to get our fifth win," Harper told Fox Cricket.

Most interesting were the comments from the Fox Cricket commentary box where former England captain Michael Vaughan made it clear how disappointed he was with the way the English hierarchy handled a nightclub incident involving Harry Brook in New Zealand before they arrived in Australia for The Ashes.

Melbourne Stars veteran Peter Siddle said "it was a good turnaround" with the win pushing the team back into second spot on the BBL table.

It's starting to heat up with three games remaining for Melbourne Renegades and two matches for Melbourne Stars.

There is still plenty of cricket left this summer so keep tuning in. Thanks for following. Can the Stars finally win the title?

Tom Rogers máhcai fas buori hámái johtilis 50:in Melbourne Renegadesa vuostá.

Melbourne Starsa veterána Peter Siddle dadjai ahte “dat lei buorre jorgaleapmi”, go dat vuoitto loktii joavkku fas nubbin sadjái BBL-tabellas.

Dál álgá garrašit, go Melbourne Renegadesas leat vel golbma spealu báhcán ja Melbourne Starsas guokte.

Dán geasi lea vel ollu cricketa báhcán, nu ahte joatkke čuovvuma. Giitu go leat mielde lean. Sáhttágo Stars loahpalaččat vuoitit namahusa?

source_doc:
Good Morning Worlds!
We are going to the tip this morning. It will clear some of the stuff we sorted yesterday from the drive. I don't think we can clear it all unless we took the trailer, but the trailer is full of steel for weighing in.
Later I might carry on packing tote crates.
#GoodMorningWorlds

Tip trip done, and another car load cleared out.
I have taken the new trailer axle, and trailer drive motor system, out of the scrap metal trailer load. That means we can get more scrap metal in there and also not accidentally weigh in the parts I want to keep.
I think, next, I will start moving the scrap steel from the back garden into the trailer so that it is ready to go.
Scrap steel prices are not very high at the moment but better than nothing, if I take enough of it in one go.
Still have to sort the non-ferrous scrap.

That thing when you are taking the rotten tyres off small, wide lawn tractor wheels....
Huge effort to unmount one side of the tyre, but it was really badly rusted tight on the other side of the rim.
In the time it took me to break the bead free, I'd forgotten I had already done the other side, and ended up with the rim free but completely inside the tyre!
I had to remount the tyre that side, and then work around it to get the rim out.
I had to cut up the inner tube to get that out too!
I wonder how many more tyres I need to unmount? Four done so far.

Mii leat mannamin ruskabáikái odne iđit. Dat veahkeha čorget eret oasi daid diŋggain maid mii eilen sortereimmet biilageainnus. In jáhke ahte mii sáhttit buot čorget eret, earret jus váldit maŋisvuojnja mielde, muhto maŋisvuojnja lea dievva stáliin mii galgá deattuhuvvot.
Maŋŋel beaivvi sáhtán joatkit tote-boksaid pakket.
#BuorreIđitMáilmmat

Ruskabáikemátki lea geargan, ja vel okta biillalasti lea čorget eret.
Leán váldán ođđa maŋisvuojnjaása ja maŋisvuojnja vuojihanmotorvuogádaga eret romemetálla-lasttas. Dat mearkkaša ahte mii sáhttit bidjat doppe vel eanet romemetálla sisa, ja seammás ii šatta deattuhuvvot oasit maid háliidan seailluhit.

Romestála hattiid eai leat dál hui allat, muhto dat lea buoret go ii mihkkege, jos viežžan doarvái olu oktanaga.

Dat diŋga go leat váldimin rotnan bonjoriid eret smávva, viiddis rásseluotta-tráktora juvllain....

Imáštallan galles vel bonjoriid dárbbašan váldit eret? Njeallje leat dál geargan.

Campanīle
A #poetry thread
i.
A Roman church belfry,
gold cross reaching for clouds:
bell tolls, sets brass note free,
sings out through misty shroud,
its high peal an appeal
to the faithful long gone.
No more piety’s zeal:
many sunsetted dawns.
Its stone tower keeps watch
through the mask of dusk-rain,
skies loosing their barrage
upon roof tiles again.
🧵👇🏼
#poem #poemaday #moody #neoclassical #church #night #photography

ii.
Who pulled on the bell cord?
Lone monk in his cloister
with none left in accord.
He, grain in church oyster —
yet no cell holds his bed,
no dust stirred by his shoes,
his name never was said,
no old books that he used.
The bell rope hangs, worn, frayed,
gnawed by church mice’s teeth.
It’s been long since it swayed,
pulled by hands underneath.
🧵👇🏼

iii.
The night wind whispers psalms
and breathes canticles’ chant
to swing the clapper of bronze,
I answer in descant —
but not with my own voice.
The wind swallows my call,
chimes its own holy noise
with the hands of its squall.
✋🏼🧵

Campanīle
Diktaráidu #poetry
i.
Romalaš girkotoardna,
golleruossa mii joksá balvvaide:
gila dárustuvvá, rábasta veaikešuoŋa,
lávlu balvagova čađa,
dan alla jietna lea ávžžuhus
oskolaččaide geat leat guhká vádjolan.
Ii šat oskku áhkkárvuohta:
máŋga iđitčuovgga mat leat lasket luoitán.
Dan geađgetoardna gáhtti fákta
litna skábmaarvvi duohken,
almit luoitaleame sin dárustusa
dáhkegeađggiid ala fas.
🧵👇🏼
#poem #poemaday #moody #neoclassical #church #night #photography

ii.
Gii giesii gila bátti?
Oktonas muŋka iežas kloastaris
mas ii oktage leat šat ovttamielas.
Son, gordni girku oastaris —
liikká ii oktage latnja ane su seaŋgga,
ii makkárge doavdi lihkahuvvon su gápmagiiguin,
su namma ii goasge daddjon,
eai dološ girjjit maid son geavahii.
Gila báddi heaŋgá, gollan, ráhkanan,
girku sáhpániid bálkkaid nálon.
Lea guhká go dat lihkahuvvui,
gieđaid geassun daid vuolde.
🧵👇🏼

iii.
Idjabiegga savkala sálmmaid
ja vuoigŋá lávlagiid šuoŋaid
liktehit veaikegila njuovčča,
mun vástidan diskaŋttas —
muhto in iežan jienain.
Biegga njiellá mu rávkama,
skilla iežas bassi jienaid
iežas stoanddu gieđaiguin.
✋🏼🧵

@JugglingWithEggs at least in my friend circle mobile phones not uncommon from early 90s, but they cost a *lot* to call from a landline (so if you were living at home your parents would discourage it), and until 1995-1999 were insecure, anyone with a radio scanner could (and often did) listen to them.
Whilst radio scanners were out of the price range of youths, many older folk had them, and until late 90s were often the kind of radio enthusiast who was a Tory bootlicker and supported the Police and other Establishment organisations, so you if discussing anything subversive on a mobile phone you risked being grassed up..
Ironically the tide turned by late 90s when scanners became affordable, and the Police were still on analogue radios 😁

@JugglingWithEggs by late 1990s everyone had a mobile phone and calls were cheaper (often with a good amount of free minutes) but SMS messages were unreliable and initially didn't even work across networks - people actually talked to each other on them!
One difference was access to physical spaces wasn't as heavily controlled as today - even though there was still CCTV and locals would call old bill on youths "hanging around", there was neither sufficient boots on the ground nor interconnected CCTV (a real security guard had to watch the footage locally, and property owners generally didn't want to pay for these folk at evenings and weekends.
There were also fewer cops on duty in outer suburbs during nights/weekends - they were all deployed into the town centres)

@vfrmedia
I remember texts sometimes taking hours to come through in the early noughties - so not always great for making on the fly arrangements.
Living in market town definitely meant less cctv and coppers back in 90’s. Remember difference when heading out into Bournemouth or Norwich of an evening. But young people having fun wasn’t frowned upon like it is now. My earlier post about facial recognition was about area where there has been uptick in teens just hanging out.

High Noon review - Billy Crudup brings classic Hollywood western back with a bang

How do you turn a classic Hollywood western into West End musical fare? Add songs, many of Bruce Springsteen's in this case, along with a few rounds of line dancing and a sizzling star in Billy Crudup. Still, it's an odd experience initially as Thea Sharrock's production switches from one brief filmic scene to the next, and the endeavour seems as wooden as the clapboard saloon-bar slats that comprise the handsome set.

As a piece of theatre, it finds its flow. As a debate play, though, it gathers a locomotive energy as it travels towards the showdown between Frank Miller (James Doherty), who is returning to this "dirty little village in the middle of nowhere," and the marshal Will Kane (Crudup) who put him behind bars. That is mostly because of the uncanny and urgent relevance of this 1952 film about a community working out (or rather, squirming out of) its civic responsibilities around institutional wrongdoing.

Originally an allegory of McCarthyism (its screenwriter, Carl Foreman, was blacklisted), the story sets the cowardice of the many against the courage of the few - in this case, the lone, heroic Kane, who mobilises his defence against Miller and his henchmen after being let down by the townsfolk. The film was blasted by John Wayne as un-American for its critical portrait of the community; the production comes to life in its arguments on collective in/action and seems to speak directly about the dilemmas facing the cowboy country of Trump's America (the shooting in Minneapolis just the latest example). Eric Roth's script uses many lines from Foreman's screenplay but fleshes out the debates on the ethical stance of a community in the face of wrongdoing and misguided American myths around immigration.

Cowardice of the many, courage of the few ... cast of High Noon. Photograph: Johan Persson

There is also the joint talent of Crudup and the ever agile Denise Gough who play the central couple on their wedding day. She is Amy Fowler, a Quaker who abhors the actions of violent men; he is the marshal who has just given up his "tin star" to start over as a shopkeeper. That is, until news reaches town that Miller is arriving on the noon train.

Gary Cooper made the role entirely his own, his integrity comparable only to Gregory Peck's Atticus in To Kill a Mockingbird. So Crudup has his long shadow to evade. He manages to hold up the part on stage as an upstanding, earnest and increasingly desperate man. Gough makes her part grittier and more modern than that of her film counterpart, Grace Kelly. The pair are convincing as a couple although their narrow characterisation hems in the full scale of their abilities.

Several other characters seem too flimsy, from Billy Howle's deputy marshal, Harvey Pell, to Rosa Salazar's Mexican businesswoman, Helen, although the affinity between her and Amy is refreshing, and Roth gives more voice and texture to these women as a whole.

Several of Springsteen's songs bring their own American politics (from the frontier optimism of Land of Hope and Dreams to The Rising, written in response to 9/11). Some are sung a cappella, mostly by Gough, who is a strong singer, her voice emanating desolation, but she reprises I'm on Fire one too many times.

It seems like a reluctant musical at times, the songs short and thin but the percussive music and sound design are always arresting, as is the lighting, designed by Neil Austin, which brings emotional clarity and intrigue. A clock is central to Tim Hatley's set design, counting down to the train's thrilling arrival and the subsequent showdown, which manages to contain tension and drama, despite the difficulty of staging a cross-town shootout.

For all its early stiffness, it builds in momentum and there are moving moments. Ultimately, the political message speaks loudest, harnessing the McCarthyist fear of then and the Trumpian terror of today.

hypothesis:
High Noon -árvvoštallan: Billy Crudup buktá klassihkalaš Hollywood-westerna ruovttoluotta garra vuolggaiguin

Mo klassihkalaš Hollywood-western rievdaduvvo West Enda musihkalaš lávdebihttán? Dasa lasihit lávlagiid, dán háve olu Bruce Springsteena repertoáras, muhtin gieruid line dancingain ja Billy Crudupa, guhte šaddá duohta čađatnástin. Dattege álggus lea dát veaháš iešguđetlágán vásáhus, go Thea Sharrocka buvttadeapmi molsu oanehis, filmmasullasaš scenas nuppi ala, ja geahččalus orru seamma geađgás go dat fiellosalunna-lávkkit, mat ráhkadit čáppa lávdegovvádusa.

Lávdebihttán dat gávdná iežas ritmma. Debáhttalávdebihttán fas čoaggá lokomotiva lágan energiija dan mielde go dat johttá ovddos Frank Millera (James Doherty) ja maršála Will Kanea (Crudup) gaskasaš vuostálastimii. Miller lea máhccan dán “duolbman unna gilii gaskkas eai geasa geainnus”, ja Kane lea dat, guhte bijai su giddagassii. Dat lea eanemusat dan dihte go dán 1952:s ráhkaduvvon filmma fállu searvvi birra, mii geahččala čoavdit – dahje baicce geassit iežas eret – iežas siviilalaš geatnegasvuođaid institusjonála boasttuvuođa ektui, lea hui eahpedábálaččat ja áibbas áigeguovdil.

Álggoálggus dat lei McCarthyisma allegoria – dan käsikirjeaddji Carl Foreman biddjojuvvui musta listui – ja muitalus bidjá eanetlogu balleheami vuostá unnán olbmuid rohkkatvuođa. Dán háve dat lea oktoheroš Kane, guhte čoaggá iežas suodjalusa Millera ja su guimmiid vuostá maŋŋá go gili olbmot leat su vuollánan. John Wayne sivkkihii filbma eahpeamerihkalažžan dan kritihkalaš searvegova geažil; dán buvttadeapmi eallá iežas vuoruhallamiin oktasaš doaimma ja doaimmaheapme birra, ja orru hupmat njuolga daid geažilvuođaid birra, mat čuožžilit Trumpa Amerihká cowboy-riikka ovddas – Minneapolisa šibihitvuohta lea dušše maŋimuš ovdamearka. Eric Rotha käsikirja geavaha olu cealkagiid Foremana screenplayas, muhto viiddida debáhtaid searvvi etihkalaš sajádaga birra boasttuvuođa ovddas ja boastut amerikalaš máidnasiid sisafárrema birra.

Ollu olbmuid balleheapmi, unnán olbmuid rohkkatvuohta ... High Noon oassálastit. Govva: Johan Persson

Doppe lea maiddái Crudupa ja álo njuovžilis Denise Gougha oktasaš dáidu, go soai čuojahit guovddáš bárra iežaska eskemiid beaivvi. Son lea Amy Fowler, quaker, guhte vaššá veahkaválddálaš albmáid daguid; son fas lea maršála, guhte lea aiddo luobban iežas “pleahkanástti” vai álggaha ođđasit gávppálažžan. Nu lea dassážii go diehtu olaha gilii ahte Miller lea boahtimin gaskabeaivve trenain.

Gary Cooper dagai roli ollásit iežas, ja su čielga njuolggadus ja moraála sáhttet dušše buohtastahttit Gregory Pecka Atticusii To Kill a Mockingbirdis. Danne lea Crudupas guhkes suoivva, man son ferte garvit. Son birge guoddit roli lávddis njuolga, duođalaš ja ain eanet heahteduvvan almmájin. Gough dahká iežas oasi garraibun ja ođđaseappot go su filmmasullasaš vuostásaš, Grace Kelly. Soai leat jáhkehahtti bárračoahkkimin, vaikko sudnu gáržžes persovdnagovvadeapmi geahpeda olles viidodaga, maid sudnu dáiddut livčče sáhttán buktit ovdan.

Máŋga eará persovdna orrot menddo geahpasat, Billy Howlea vuollemaršála Harvey Pellas Rosa Salazara meksikolaš fitnodatnissona Helenii. Dattege son ja Amy gaskasaš lahkašvuohta lea ođasmahtti, ja Roth addá dainna nissonolbmuide oppalaččat eanet jiena ja ivnni.

Máŋga Springsteena lávlaga buktet secce iežaset amerikalaš politihka, Land of Hope and Dreamsa rádjeguovllu optimisma rájes gitta The Risingii, mii čállojuvvui 9/11 maŋŋá. Muhtumat lávlojit a cappella, eanemusat Gough bokte, guhte lea nanus lávlejeaddji; su jietna guhkoda guorusvuođa, muhto son máhcaha I’m on Fire -lávlagii veahá menddo dávjá.

Muhtumin dát orru veaháš vuosteháli musihkalan: lávlagat leat oanehat ja geahppát, muhto perkušuvdnalaš musihkka ja jietnahábmen leat álo geassevaččat. Seamma guoská Neil Austina hábmehan čuovgadeapmái, mii buktá dovdduide čielggasvuođa ja geassevuođa. Diibmu lea guovddážis Tim Hatley lávdegovvádusas, lohkamin maŋosága trenna geahččalmas olahussii ja dan maŋŋá boahtte vuostálastimii, mii seailluha jietnama ja dráma, vaikko lea váttis lávddistit gili rastá šibihitvuođa.

Danne lea Crudupas guhkes suoivva, man son ferte garvit. Son birge guoddit roli lávddis njuolga, duođalaš ja ain eanet heahteduvvan almmájin. Gough dahká iežas oasi garraibun ja ođđaseappot go su filmmasullasaš vuostásaš, Grace Kelly. Soai leat jáhkehahtti bárračoahkkimin, vaikko sudnu gáržžes persovdnagovvadeapmi geahpeda olles viidodaga, maid sudnu dáiddut livčče sáhttán buktit ovdan.

Máŋga eará persovdna orrot menddo geahpasat, Billy Howlea vuollemaršála Harvey Pellas Rosa Salazara meksikolaš fitnodatnissona Helenii. Dattege son ja Amy gaskasaš lahkašvuohta lea ođasmahtti, ja Roth addá dainna nissonolbmuide oppalaččat eanet jiena ja ivnni.

Muhtumat lávlojit a cappella, eanemusat Gough bokte, guhte lea nanus lávlejeaddji; su jietna guhkoda guorusvuođa, muhto son máhcaha I’m on Fire -lávlagii veahá menddo dávjá.

Muhtumin dát orru veaháš vuosteháli musihkalan: lávlagat leat oanehat ja geahppát, muhto perkušuvdnalaš musihkka ja jietnahábmen leat álo geassevaččat. Seamma guoská Neil Austina hábmehan čuovgadeapmái, mii buktá dovdduide čielggasvuođa ja geassevuođa. Diibmu lea guovddážis Tim Hatley lávdegovvádusas, lohkamin maŋosága trenna geahččalmas olahussii ja dan maŋŋá boahtte vuostálastimii, mii seailluha jietnama ja dráma, vaikko lea váttis lávddistit gili rastá šibihitvuođa.

Vaikko álggus lea geađgásvuohta, dat hukse iežas fárrui ja doppe leat maiddái liikodihtti bottut. Loahpas lea dat politihkalaš diehtu, mii čuojaha garraseamosit, go dat čatná oktii dalleáigásaš McCarthy-balu ja odnebeaivvi trumpalaš botkkaldaga.

as you all know, I'm a deeply religious person 🛐 so..
the scene: we're in the garden of eden. adam is eating apples from the forbidden tree, because of course he is. eve is having none of his shit, grabs an unfortunate unsuspecting nearby serpent, and is about to whip the shit out of adam. 🐍
#painting

painting with bazkie! 🧵 a (slow) thread [2/x]
so, we're gonna need reference photos. I want eve to be in the process of swinging the serpent around; so then I figured a baseball batter would be a good fit.
so wading through the AI slop, I found this actual photo that has a nice pose and good lighting.

painting with bazkie! 🧵 a (slow) thread [3/x]

took about 20 pics with slightly different in stances etc., and decided on this one. (the right hand is going to hold the apple)

Arthur Okonkwo's penalty shootout heroics causes FA Cup shock as Wrexham beat Nottingham Forest

Wrexham won an FA Cup third-round thriller in front of Hollywood owner Ryan Reynolds as Nottingham Forest were dumped out of the competition on penalties after a 3-3 draw.

Arthur Okonkwo was the Wrexham hero with stops from Igor Jesus and Omari Hutchinson giving them a 4-3 victory on spot-kicks after Josh Windass, Callum Doyle, George Thomason and Jay Rodriguez had converted from the spot.

First-half goals from Liberato Cacace and Oliver Rathbone gave Wrexham early control and had Reynolds trading high fives and hugs from his vantage point in the main stand.

Jesus cut the deficit before Dominic Hyam's diving header restored Wrexham's two-goal advantage with 16 minutes remaining.

Forest looked dead and buried but substitute Callum Hudson-Odoi produced two outstanding finishes, the equaliser coming in the 89th minute.

Wrexham have won three successive promotions to go from non-league to the Championship, but this was the first time since being taken over by Reynolds and fellow actor Rob Mac nearly five years ago they had met Premier League opposition.

Forest made eight changes after beating West Ham on Tuesday, with goalkeeper Matz Sels, Jesus and Hutchinson remaining and Wales international Neco Williams on a stacked bench at his local club.

Callum Hudson-Odoi came off the bench and scored twice to force the match to penalties (REUTERS)

Kieffer Moore was not risked after injury as Wrexham sought to extend a four-game winning streak that had taken them a point from the Championship play-off places.

Forest started on the front front with Jesus shooting over and Douglas Luiz found the net after 17 minutes.

Referee Paul Tierney initially awarded the goal, but then ruled it out after deciding Luiz had controlled the ball with his arm before volleying home.

Wrexham had been tidy in possession without a cutting edge but that was to change in the final 10 minutes of the first half.

Ollie Rathbone doubled Wrexham's lead after Liberato Cacace's opener (REUTERS)

Sam Smith dragged wide before Cacace took advantage after 37 minutes to drive home his maiden Wrexham goal from 20 yards aided by the faintest of deflections off Morato's heel.

Wrexham smiles were even wider three minutes later as Rathbone broke through Morato's challenge to fire in his third goal in four games.

It should have been three - and possibly contest over - when Smith scampered through the Forest half unchecked but failed to beat Sels" outstretched leg.

Forest boss Sean Dyche made a triple substitution at half-time with Williams, Morgan Gibbs-White and Nicolas Dominguez sent on to salvage the situation.

Okonkwo saved the decisive penalty to deny Omari Hutchinson in the shootout (Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

The visitors were instantly more fluid as Okonkwo tipped over Luiz's free-kick and kept out Nicolo Savona's strike.

Sels saved well from Broadhead but Forest were in the ascendancy and struck when Savona set up the leaping Jesus for a header that hit the post and just about crossed the line.

The drama rose as Hyam headed in a superb George Dobson free-kick and Hudson-Odoi swept home 60 seconds later to set up a grandstand finish.

Hudson-Odoi took the tie into extra time in fantastic fashion, taking a touch on his chest and lofting a perfect volley over Okonkwo, but Wrexham were not to be denied their first top-flight FA Cup scalp for 26 years.

Sean Dyche made eight changes to the Forest side and called on his first choice players but couldn't get over the line (Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Elsewhere in the FA Cup, Oxford United advanced to the fourth round with a 4-3 penalty shootout win over MK Dons and Port Vale defeated Fleetwood 1-0.

Wigan Athletic also progressed after a superb display at Deepdale saw the League One side beat Championship play-off chasers Preston North End 1-0 as well.

Arthur Okonkwo lei Wrexhama sáŋgar. Son bissehii Igor Jesusa ja Omari Hutchinsona spáppaid ja dasto nannii 4–3-vuoittu spáppagastvimiiguin maŋŋel go Josh Windass, Callum Doyle, George Thomason ja Jay Rodriguez ledje skoren iežaset gastimiid.

Vuosttaš lađi málat, maid Liberato Cacace ja Oliver Rathbone skorejeigga, adde Wrexhamii jođihanposišuvnna álggus, ja Reynolds modjui, fálai "high five" -vuollánemiid ja fáhtestalai váldotribynas.

Jesus unnidii erohusa ovdal go Dominic Hyama njuikejeaddji oaivečaskku buvttii Wrexhama guovttemállo-jođihusa ruovttoluotta go 16 minuhta ledje báhcán speallat.

Forest orrui leat juo gárvves, muhto sadjásaš spálli Callum Hudson-Odoi skorii guokte earenoamáš mála, main dássehusmálla bođii 89. minuhtas.

Wrexham lea vuoitán golbma maŋŋálas loktenortnega non-league-gilvvus gitta Championship-dássái, muhto dát lei vuosttaš gearddi dan maŋŋel go Reynolds ja su neavttárustibi Rob McElhenney válde badjelasaset joavkku lagabui vihtta jagi áigi, go sii deaivvadedje Premier League-joavkkuin.

Forest dagahii gávcci rievdadusa maŋŋel go ledje vuoitán West Hama maŋŋebárgga. Uksavahtto Matz Sels, Jesus ja Hutchinson bázze dán speallái, ja Walesa riikkajoavkkospálli Neco Williams lei sadjásaččaid beavddis báikkálaš klubbastis.

Callum Hudson-Odoi bođii sadjásažžan ja skorii guktii, mii doalvui spealu spáppagastvimiidda (REUTERS)

Kieffer Mooreain ii váldojuvvon riska maŋŋel rasiiduvvama go Wrexham geahččalii viiddidit njealje spealu vuoitoráiddu, mii lei doalvun sin ovtta čuoggá lagabui Championshipa play-off-sajiide.

Forest álggahii garrasit go Jesus bálkestii spáppa badjel, ja Douglas Luiz gávnnai mállo-neatji 17 minuhta maŋŋel.

Duopmar Paul Tierney mieđhii álggos mála, muhto gielddi dan dasto go gávnnahii ahte Luiz lei stivren spáppa gieđainis ovdal go faskkii dan sisa.

Wrexham lei leamaš čorgat spáppa badjelis muhto dasto váillui badjelmearálaš ávki, muhto dat rievddai vuosttaš lađi maŋimuš 10 minuhtas.

Sam Smith geasii spáppa viidát ovdal go Cacace geavahii ávkki 37 minuhta maŋŋel ja faskkii iežas vuosttaš Wrexham-mála 20 mehtera duohken vehkiin veháža maŋŋel Morato juolggi duohken.

Wrexham-modjit ledje vel eanet viidát golbma minuhta maŋŋel go Rathbone rikki Morato hástalusa ja bálkestii iežas goalmmát mála njealje spealus.

Dat galggai leat golbma - ja soaitá vel gilvu loahpahuvvon - go Smith faskkii jođánit Foresta beallái almmá goasii oktage easttaleami muhto ii nagadan vuoitit Selsa guhkiduvvon juolggi.

Forest-hoavda Sean Dyche dagahii golmma rievdadusa lađđagaskkas go Williams, Morgan Gibbs-White ja Nicolas Dominguez sáddejuvvojedje gidtet dili.

Okonkwo gájui mearrideaddji spáppa go son bissehii Omari Hutchinsona spáppagastvimiin (Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Galledeaddjit ledje dakkaviđe eanet njuovžilat go Okonkwo bálkestii badjel Luiza nuvttáspárttu ja doalai eret Nicolo Savona faskkideami.

Sels gájui bures Broadheada spárttu muhto Forest lei badjánis ja časkkii go Savona ordni njuikejeaddji Jesusii oaivespárttuin mii časkkii stággui ja nu dasto badjel mállo-sárgá.

Dramatihka lassánii go Hyam oaivvásti eallálaččat George Dobsona fiidna nuvttáspárttu sisa ja Hudson-Odoi časkkii sisa 60 sekundda maŋŋel ja dagahii fámolaš loahpaheami.

Hudson-Odoi doalvun gaskaspealu lassiáigái earenoamáš vugiin, válddedettiinis spáppa raddái ja faskkiidis earenoamáš buori spárttu Okonkwo badjel, muhto Wrexham ii bággejuvvon iežaset vuosttaš top-flight FA Cup vuoittus 26 jahkái.

Sean Dyche dagahii gávcci rievdadusa Forest-joavkkus ja gohčui iežas vuosttašvuođu-spálliid muhto ii nagadan beassat badjel mállo-sárgá (Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Eará sajis FA Cupas, Oxford United manai viidáseappot njealját gierdui 4–3 spáppagastvingilvvu vuoittuin MK Donsa badjel ja Port Vale vuittii Fleetwooda 1–0.

Wigan Athletic maid manai viidáseappot maŋŋel earenoamáš buori spealu Deepdaleis gos League One -joavku vuittii Championshipa play-off-hástaleaddji Preston North Enda maid 1–0.

- how bridge works

source_doc:
Ironing the lightweight green corduroy for my first try at the Sachi's Studio Newsboy Cap pattern. I don't know how I feel about the recommendation to use interfacing but it probably does want something to stiffen and thicken it a bit.
#millinery

Sachi's newsboy cap pattern advises to cut the crown pieces diagonal to the weave ("on the bias") to allow more stretch around the circumference but that will make the corduroy rows run aslant, where I prefer them vertical.
We shall see. This is the test cookie to get a feel for the pattern. I like corduroy for texture but green wouldn't be my first choice, and this fabric is lightweight enough that I should add a layer, whether interfacing or what-have-you from the stash.

On a second look, my fabric isn't corduroy at all, it's just velvet, so I can cut at 45° to the fabric weave like Sachi suggests in the Newsboy Cap pattern and it won't look strange.
#millinery
